sahneler.metin: A trading firm's computers started sending runaway stock orders.
Within minutes, the company had lost hundreds of millions of dollars.
New software had been installed the night before.
It was deployed by hand to eight servers.
A reused setting woke up long-dead code on that machine.
There was no automatic kill switch.
The firm had to be rescued and sold.

aciklama:
Knight Capital lost hundreds of millions of dollars in minutes. The cause: a reused flag reactivating obsolete trading code on a server that didn't get the new software.

#shorts #engineering #software
soru: Should everything have a kill switch?

vaka.yanilgi: No hacker was involved. A manual deployment missed one server, and old code woke up.
vaka.tartisma: There was no automatic kill switch. Should every automated system have one?
